answer: Unfortunately, no. The older notarized form NW-POA-1 was replaced by NW-POA-2 on February 1, 2026, and an NW-POA-1 signed before that date is only accepted until June 30, 2026, so it won't be valid for your July 10 appointment. Your mom can sign the new form NW-POA-2 instead, which can be signed electronically with no notary. The exception is Georgia, where a power of attorney, including NW-POA-2, must still be notarized.
